title: First 'Nature Listening Festival' Held in Finland
paragraphs: Most music festivals are loud and crowded. But a new festival in Finland is the complete opposite. It is called Hiljaa Fest, and it describes itself as the world's first "Festival of Nature Listening."

"Hiljaa" means "quietly" in Finnish, and some people have nicknamed the event "Quietchella," a joke referring to Coachella, the famous music festival in California. Instead of bands and singers, the "performers" at this festival come from nature.

The festival is being held at Valkmusa National Park in Pyhtää, in southern Finland, about 90 minutes east of Helsinki. The park is known for its wetlands, called mires, which contain around 40 different types of habitat. Visitors can walk along wooden boardwalks and climb observation towers to enjoy the landscape.

According to the organizers, there are 13 natural "acts" spread across four different "stages" around the park. The performers include black grouse, which are birds known for their unusual calls, as well as cranes, the wind and moss. The festival's official symbol is a rare moth that lives in the park. However, the organizers warn that some performers are less predictable than others, so visitors cannot be sure that every act will appear. There is no schedule.

The festival opened on October 10 with a special event for 30 people chosen by lottery. After that, it is open to everyone for free as a self-guided experience until October 31. Visitors are asked to follow Finland's outdoor rules, which means respecting nature and leaving no trace. Because the route uses boardwalks and forest paths, the organizers say it is not yet suitable for people who use mobility aids.

The purpose of the festival is to encourage people to slow down and notice the small details of the natural world. Simo Peri, the festival's creative director and a wilderness guide, described it as a festival trip designed to nurture one's soul and mind.
If this year's festival is successful, it could return in 2027.
